title: To-do manager with priorities and JSON persistence
prompt:
Build a to-do list manager in Python.

Modules:
- models.py: a dataclass `Task` with fields `id: int`, `title: str`, `priority: int`, `done: bool = False`.
- todo_list.py: `class TodoList`.
  - `add(title, priority=2)` creates a Task and returns it. Ids start at 1 and increase by 1 for each new task. Raises `ValueError` if the title is empty or only whitespace, or if priority is not 1, 2 or 3.
  - `complete(task_id)` marks the task done; raises `KeyError` for an unknown id.
  - `remove(task_id)` deletes the task; raises `KeyError` for an unknown id.
  - `pending()` returns the tasks that are not done, sorted by priority (1 first) and then by id.
  - `save(path)` writes all tasks to a JSON file.
  - `TodoList.load(path)` (a classmethod) reads that file and returns a TodoList with the same tasks; ids of tasks added after loading continue from the highest loaded id.
- main.py: command-line interface. Read commands from standard input, one per line, until `quit` or end of input:
  - `add <priority> <title words...>` prints `Added task <id>`
  - `done <id>` marks a task done
  - `list` prints each pending task on its own line as `<id>. [P<priority>] <title>`
  - On any error print a line starting with `Error:` and continue.

Constraints: use only the Python standard library. The entry point is main.py in the project root, guarded by `if __name__ == "__main__":`.
